clues.text: The first production of this was choreographed by Lev Ivanov after Marius Pepita became ill, and for it the composer had a celeste brought in secret from Germany.
A trio of exotic dances in this ballet’s second act representing chocolate, tea, and coffee has received scrutiny for its cultural insensitivity.
This work opens with the title item given as a gift by Drosselmeyer; it is later broken by Fritz.
This ballet’s notable use of the celesta required its composer to smuggle one in from Germany.
This work contains a Spanish dance representing chocolate and an Arabian dance representing coffee, and it also contains a “Waltz of the Snowflakes.”
In this ballet, a little girl is able to use her slipper to ward off the nefarious Mouse King.

Based on a story by E.T.A. Hoffman, it sees a girl dream of characters such as Mother Ginger, the Snow Queen, and Arabian Coffee, who are inspired by food items at a party where that girl, Clara, receives the title gift from Count Drosselmeyer.
In this ballet, a kingdom named The Land of Sweets is ruled by the Sugar Plum Fairy, who is visited by Clara.
The Waltz of the Snowflakes and Dance of the Sugarplum Fairy appear in what Peter Tchaikovsky ballet about Clara's Christmas gift coming to life?
The title toy becomes a prince in what Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky ballet set during Christmas?
This musician’s recording of “Heebie Jeebies” supposedly introduced scat singing, though there is evidence of the form predating that recording by fifteen years.
One blues song by this artist includes a stop-time clarinet solo based on tap-dancing in Chicago’s Sunset Cafe.
This musician once added the lyrics "Oh, memory" before an instrumental break in a rendition of the Hoagy Carmichael song "Stardust".
This musician was originally a member of the Creole band in Chicago along with his mentor Joe King Oliver.
This man's all-stars included Jack Teagarden and Trummy Young.
This musician who repopularized King Oliver’s “West End Blues” sings in another song, “I see trees of green, red roses too” in his trademark gravelly voice.
He recorded a 1964 performance of "Hello Dolly," in addition to claiming to hear "friends shaking hands...saying how do you do."
On the song “Heebie Jeebies,” this musician first utilized his signature scat singing style, and on a different song, this man describes “trees of green / red roses too.”
Satchmo was this man's nickname, and he frequently used wordless syllables called scat singing.
Name this jazz trumpeter from New Orleans.

answerlines: Richard Strauss [prompt on Strauss; do NOT accept or prompt on “Johann Strauss”]

clues.text: This composer wanted the Wagnerian soprano Kirsten Flagstad to premiere a set of songs which were collected posthumously by his friend Ernst Roth.
This composer set the poems “When Falling Asleep” and “At Sunset” to music in one work.
Georg Solti conducted a final act trio from one of this composer’s operas at his funeral; that trio is followed by the love duet “Ist ein Traum.”
In the second movement of a piece by this composer, tubas play a four-note motif in parallel fifths to represent “adversaries” of the title character.
This composer wrote an Olympic Hymn for the Berlin Olympics in 1936.
His own opera Feuersnot was given in 1901, before the premier of a work, regarded as blasphemous, based on a play by Oscar Wilde.
A “Works of Peace” movement is included in a piece by this composer used to portray a hero’s life, Ein Heldenleben.

A 22 movement tone poem by this composer includes a “Peak” motif to portray the title mountain range; that motif was inspired by another piece by this composer which uses the rising notes “C, G, C” to illustrate sunrise.
Sophie falls in love with Octavian, who delivers her a silver rose, in an opera by what German composer of Salome and Der Rosenkavalier?
Name this German composer of the opera Salome and an homage to Friedrich Nietzsche, Thus Spake Zarathustra.
